conversationalSummary.text: TODAY there isn’t a reliable window, so it’s probably not worth the drive. Meio da Baia is the best available option on paper, but the wind angle is off and the gusts could make it messy, so it may feel too soft unless the swell really shows up clean. I’d check Surfline and the MEO Beachcam before leaving—only go if the cams look noticeably better than expected; otherwise, save it for another day.

best.explanation: Meio da Baia looks like a fun-sized window for Too soft, Low confidence: 0.6-1.1 m, 52 kJ, 6 s period, workable consistency 61/100, and wind is the main risk.  An inconsistent Baía spot that can work well when north-northwest swell reaches the bay; this is best for bodyboard sessions when the bay is clean, there is enough period and size, and the forecast shows a defined wave; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot; Meio da Baia may feel too soft without more push; gusts over 35 km/h could make it messy.
best.shortExplanation: Meio da Baia is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  It looks too soft to make the drive worthwhile.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide and timing are lining up well for this spot.

ranked.explanation: Baleal looks like a small window for Too soft, Low confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 30 kJ, 7 s period, lully 19/100, and wind is the main risk.  A broad, forgiving beach setup with several peaks; this is best for spreading out and finding a manageable wave when the bay has enough push; worth keeping on the radar because Surfline is showing it above Poor while most other local spots are Poor..  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; spot surf looks too small; wind angle is poor for this spot; 6-9s at mid tide is soft and sectiony on the Baleal sandbanks; Baleal looks below your bodyboard fun size; Baleal may feel too soft without more push.
